See resource/heat limitations and Help for user controls.

docs.title: Install and contribute
docs.text: RoTab is distributed as a private unpacked Chromium extension. An authorized build can be loaded through Chrome or Brave's extension developer page. The documented interface is 0.5.6; the packaged shared-TURN pilot is 0.5.2. Current capabilities distinguishes their validation records. Illustrated Help describes the controls.

docs.title: Volunteer for a submitted protein
docs.text:
1. Network discovery starts automatically. The green Histidine/status indicator means a network connection is live; it does not mean a model is already running.
  2. Choose Start volunteering in the simple protein widget or dashboard. This one click enables future compatible assignments; no connection settings are required. Pause new tasks stops accepting more work while the current model finishes.
  3. Available campaigns show title, protocol, queue information and the sender's mandatory short description. Contribute still accepts one model without enabling automatic work.
  4. The accepted protein appears in the molecular view. Its actual WASM snapshots drive the current/best energy and graph. Score-only tasks remain structurally static; optimization/design motion depends on the method.

The simple new-tab view retains the protein widget while computation runs. Returning to the dashboard restores its graphs and retained frames without starting another calculation. Computation settings → Live demonstration → Try FastRelax · sample protein starts a separate bundled demo when the session is available.

The computing tab has a histidine outline favicon: green for connected, pulsing green for research computation, yellow for a local benchmark/demo, gray for disconnected idle, and red for an error. Other tabs keep the same outline in a fixed gray. A reduced-motion preference disables pulsing. All tabs are titled RoTab. Linked tabs can start or pause volunteering without becoming a second coordinator; Go to main tab in Computation settings focuses the computing tab. When it closes, the next coordinator takes over the colored favicon.

The histidine beside RoTab in the page header uses those status colors in every tab, including linked tabs. Its pulse indicates research computation. There is no separate header status dot.

docs.title: Publish a target
docs.text:
Open the paper-plane Volunteer network panel. Upload a supported protein, select a method, provide a title and a description of 1 to 240 characters, choose the independent model count and starting seed, then submit. The campaign schema permits up to 1,000 model attempts. Each attempt runs the method's fixed work budget using its own seed; the model count does not change FastRelax repeats.

The publisher's browser stores the campaign before advertising it. Online compatible volunteers are discovered automatically; manual pairing is an advanced fallback rather than the normal submission step. Keep the publisher tab online to assign models and receive results. A submitted campaign can wait locally with no volunteers connected, then schedule when peers become available. Also calculate on this browser is checked by default: the publisher runs independent models alongside volunteers. Uncheck it for a coordinator-only campaign. Each browser runs one network assignment at a time; extra models wait for available participants.

The campaign panel distinguishes observed devices, ready volunteers, assignments waiting to start, and live running models. Each active model shows its worker, reported progress and latest energy when available. Updates come from the assigned browser, not estimated activity; stale telemetry is marked as awaiting an update.

Results retain campaign/attempt IDs, publisher/volunteer identities, seed, protocol, source/engine/data hashes and output hashes. The queue fences superseded/cancelled leases and deduplicates matching returned results; a delayed result can succeed while its token remains current. Export input, outputs and experiment records before removing local data. A received result remains scientifically unverified in the interface. Assignment architecture.

docs.title: Local demonstrations and benchmarks
docs.text:
The live FastRelax demo uses packaged 1L2Y coordinates. The replay view uses previously recorded real frames and is explicitly playback. Offline import/export is available in computation settings for supported coordinate benchmarks. Neither the demo nor a local benchmark is an official Rosetta@home contribution.

A plain PDB import starts with Fixed-coordinate scoring. It evaluates the structure, saves initial/final snapshots, and completes without running relaxation. An unchanged structure and flat energy graph are expected for this method. In Computation settings → Calculation protocol, select Torsion FastRelax to optimize the imported protein; the selector applies to the imported target as well as bundled inputs. A completed imported Score also offers Run FastRelax. This starts a new run on the currently imported target, using the imported structure.

The next-run protocol choice persists locally. It does not change an active or paused checkpoint, previous results or the original protocol and reference declared by benchmark JSON. Exports record the executed protocol for each model; results from a different protocol are not labelled comparable to the original reference. Larger inputs can require substantially more time and memory. Successful large-input scoring does not establish FastRelax support for the same input. See memory and verification scope.

Residue-energy colors read the weighted total column in each snapshot's Rosetta PDB energy table. The viewer maps the pinned standard residue types HIS_D to PDB HIS, and CYZ to CYS, including terminal variants, while retaining pose-ordinal and sequence-identity validation. A malformed/mismatched table remains unavailable rather than supplying guessed scores. Saved scored structures can be recolored after an extension update without rerunning Rosetta.

CPU worker count and per-worker intensity are local controls. Publishers cannot override them or enable automatic continuation remotely. Automatic acceptance starts off; Start volunteering explicitly enables it. Pausing terminates active scientific workers; completed models are retained, and unfinished models restart from their recorded seeds on resume.

docs.title: New-tab features
docs.text:
New installations use the simple view and light Doodle appearance. Appearance is separate from computation settings and includes dark/system variants, optional Doodle molecular rendering, local font stacks, custom accent, highlight and background colors, gradients and uploaded backgrounds. Accent colors charts and progress; highlights color selections and interaction states with theme-aware contrast. Highlights follow the accent unless a separate color is saved. Favorites support folders and zero to three configurable rows; fresh installs start with two, with the second using frequent sites when available. Hover over the favorites area (or focus it with the keyboard) to show add, folder and configuration controls. In configuration, edit/remove favorite tiles and folders directly from the simple view, including the bundled Google folder. Removing a folder keeps its links in the main list; removing a favorite deletes that link. An empty row list persists across new tabs and reloads.

Appearance → Opening view chooses the preferred layout for newly opened tabs. Opening the protein dashboard or returning to the simple view changes only the current tab. Other open tabs retain their layouts, and the next new tab opens in the saved preferred layout. Choosing an opening layout in Appearance previews it in the tab where it was selected.

OK closes Appearance and confirms valid connection/settings changes; X remains available. Many settings apply immediately, while forms retain their explicit Save/Create actions. Appearance also offers Google search suggestions, off by default. Enabling it sends typed queries after a short debounce. Disabling it stops suggestion requests; normal Google search remains available. The suggestion endpoint is not a guaranteed public API, so failures silently fall back to ordinary search.

The greeting follows the device's local clock: morning from 05:00, afternoon from 12:00, evening from 18:00 and night from 22:00 until 05:00. It updates while the tab stays open.

Weather attempts browser location once, then asks for a city if detection fails or is declined. It has no preset city; choices persist locally. Device coordinates are rounded to two decimal places. A cached browser-side Photon/OpenStreetMap lookup adds the city to the label, for example Current location - Geneva; older unnamed device locations are resolved too. If naming fails, Current location and its forecast remain usable. Click the location label to change city or retry detection. Forecast coordinates go to Open-Meteo; rounded device coordinates also go to Photon for city naming, never to volunteer peers. Forecasts are cached and offer configurable multi-day expansion. The compact card shows available wind, humidity, daily rain chance and local sunrise/sunset times. Missing readings are omitted. Expanded forecasts leave space between the low temperatures and footer. Weather fields. Chromium requires a declared location permission for extension pages. Chrome location behavior, Photon service.

Calendar supports local events and optional Google Calendar integration after OAuth configuration. The simple-view tiles use shared row heights and a dense responsive grid: the protein stays first, while weather, calendar, queue and Pomodoro can be moved, resized or hidden.

Use the gear in the calendar widget's top toolbar, beside move, resize and hide, to enable Gregorian, Shamsi (Persian solar), or Qamari (Hijri lunar) calendars. Choose One calendar to place their dates together, with a primary calendar controlling the month and navigation, or Separate widgets for independent native months. Alternate day numbers share one line in the order shown by the legend, keeping date cells the same height with one, two or three calendars. Press OK to apply. These controls stay in the calendar widget; Appearance and computation settings do not contain them.

Qamari offers Civil (tabular) and Umm al-Qura calculations. These are calculated calendars, so a local moon-sighting date may differ. Conversion uses the browser's Intl.DateTimeFormat calendar support, without a service or installation. Local notes and Google events remain tied to the same civil date in every view. Event editors label their date fields Gregorian and show the equivalent enabled dates. Google event queries cover the displayed native month, including both Gregorian months when needed.

Click the Pomodoro minutes or seconds to edit hours, minutes and seconds directly; save with the tick or start immediately. Zero hours are omitted from the countdown. A shared browser deadline survives hiding the widget or opening the dashboard. A progress ring appears around the tab favicon, and one two-note chime plays at completion across open tabs after Start/Resume unlocks browser audio. Reloading an already-completed timer does not replay the chime. Sound depends on the browser permitting audio and at least one audio-enabled RoTab remaining open. Chrome audio policy.

The protein-style Pomodoro is a timer visualization; it must not be counted as a scientific model or volunteer contribution. These widgets do not change Rosetta's methods.

docs.title: Connectivity troubleshooting
docs.text: Use the same network protocol/build, room and at least one shared reachable relay. Distinguish relay connection from direct WebRTC connection and scientific engine initialization. Different networks can fail to establish a direct route; the network page explains STUN/TURN and what remains to be tested. The last RoTab's closure stops browser calculation rather than leaving an installed daemon running.

docs.title: Help
docs.text: RoTab opens in Simple view by default. The protein tile opens the detailed dashboard; the back arrow returns to Simple view. Appearance stores the preferred opening layout independently of the view open in another tab.

docs.title: Find a control
docs.text:
Action Control or guide Change theme, background, opening layout or search suggestions Palette icon → Appearance Add/remove favorites, folders or shortcut rows Hover/focus the favorite bar → Shortcut controls Change calendars, move/resize/hide a widget Widget's upper controls → Personal widgets Set focus duration or start a Pomodoro Click the timer's digits → Focus timer Start helping with research Dashboard → Start volunteering Submit a protein for volunteer calculation Paper-plane icon → Submit a target Rotate the molecule, inspect energy or run a local demo Protein and calculations Resolve a failed connection, missing result or memory error Troubleshooting Set up a managed TURN relay for different networks Connect across networks

OK closes a menu or confirms its form. Many settings apply immediately; Calendar settings apply on confirmation. Escape or X dismisses the menu. Submitting a scientific job, pausing new assignments and stopping an active calculation each use separate controls.

docs.title: Status indicator
docs.text:
Histidine color Meaning Green Network connection is live; no model is currently computing Pulsing green Research/volunteer computation is active Yellow Local benchmark or demo is active Gray Idle without a live network connection Red An error needs attention

The computing tab's favicon uses these states; linked tabs keep a neutral Histidine outline. The Histidine beside RoTab shows the shared status in either view. Reduced motion disables the pulsing effect. A linked tab offers Go to main tab for owner-only settings. Opening additional RoTabs in the same profile does not create extra independent volunteers.

docs.title: Illustrations
docs.text:
Screenshots use isolated browser profiles, the bundled Trp-cage reference, example weather, and controlled network fixtures. They illustrate controls and do not represent a public research campaign or establish reachability between different networks.

Data and privacy describes recipients and local storage. Architecture explains the implementation.

docs.title: Open Help from RoTab
docs.text: RoTab 0.5.6 provides Help, Privacy and Support links in Appearance and Settings. The dashboard sidebar also provides Help and documentation. These links open this website in a separate browser tab; the website does not supply executable code to the extension.

docs.title: Protein view and local calculations
docs.text: Click the protein tile or Open dashboard to enter the full view. The dashboard displays the current or reference structure, retained scientific snapshots, color controls, energy history and volunteer setup. Arrows on the left and right panel edges collapse the side panels to enlarge the protein workspace.

docs.title: View controls
docs.text:
Control Effect Smooth motion Interpolate the display between measured coordinates; does not create scientific samples Reset view Restore camera framing Automatic orbit Toggle rotation and save the same preference used in Settings Atoms/ribbon Change molecular representation Fullscreen Enlarge the molecular view Compare start / selected baseline Align another retained structure for visual comparison Color / Inspect residue Choose coloring and select a residue to inspect available data Replay this calculation Play retained measured snapshots; does not rerun the protocol

Rotation defaults on. Computation settings → Rotate protein automatically saves an off choice across tabs/reloads. Reduced motion disables it, and selecting a residue pauses it for inspection. Hidden/offscreen views skip continuous rendering.

Residue-energy colors require per-residue energy data in the selected structure. Reference/unscored inputs may use neutral colors. Color is a display of the computed metric; it is not an experimental confidence or disease annotation.

docs.title: Calculation methods
docs.text:
Score evaluates fixed coordinates. Its initial/final snapshots can look identical, and a flat two-point graph does not by itself mean a stopped calculation. Minimize or FastRelax can produce a changing optimization trajectory. Packing changes side chains; design methods can change sequence. These are bounded methods rather than arbitrary native Rosetta commands. Method catalogue.

One worker at 10% cooperative intensity is the extension default. Higher worker counts run independent models with separate memory, rather than accelerating a single model through shared cores. The intensity setting controls cooperative work/sleep periods and is not a hardware temperature cap.

docs.title: Run a local demo or imported benchmark
docs.text:
Open Computation settings → Live demonstration → Try FastRelax · sample protein for the bundled example. Under Offline benchmark, upload supported coordinate JSON/PDB/ENT or gzipped PDB data. The importer resolves supported alternate atom locations and ensembles locally and retains preparation provenance. A PDB-only benchmark defaults to Score. Select an optimization protocol for structural refinement.

Uploads are prepared as protein-only inputs. Water, non-protein ions and ligands are removed along with connectivity records that refer to them. A visible caution lists the removals before calculation; expand the input summary for details and Original PDB / Prepared PDB downloads. The original file is retained. Results exclude the removed components and their interactions, so they describe the protein alone. Modified amino acids, missing backbone atoms and additional protein chains can still require a supported input. Exact preparation policy.

The example uses bundled 20-residue coordinates with added water, zinc and a ligand. Installed Chrome and Brave upload checks confirmed visible cautions and exact original downloads; subsequent WASM Score results passed independent native rescoring. Validation summary.

There is no protein residue-count admission cap. Browser memory, stack limits, supported chemistry and the engine's database coverage still constrain real inputs. An accepted upload is not a guarantee every method will complete on it. Large protein memory.

docs.title: Startup, completion and recovery
docs.text:
Cold initialization can take minutes before the first measured snapshot. The worker loads and initializes Rosetta, then prepares and scores the structure. This stage can produce CPU bursts before cooperative throttling starts. Extension workers are recreated per model, so setup can recur. Comparative measurements have not established the cause of differing temperature and fan behavior across users' Macs.

Pause/stop an active calculation to terminate its worker. Completed models are saved. Resuming an unfinished model replays its original seed rather than continuing a full in-memory checkpoint. Pause new tasks concerns future volunteer assignments and can let the current model finish.

Workers are also terminated on completion. Saved structures, the molecular viewer and browser caches still occupy memory afterward. WASM heap reports active workers' linear memory, while UI JS heap reports the page's approximate JavaScript allocation; neither is the tab's total RAM. Memory lifetime and measured checks.

The computing tab displays a notice while a calculation is starting or running. Attempting to close, reload or leave that tab requests the browser's confirmation; canceling keeps the calculation running. Linked tabs and paused, completed, stopped or failed runs do not request this warning. Confirming departure terminates the tab's workers; another open tab may recover saved work by replaying unfinished seeds. Browsers supply the confirmation wording and require prior interaction with the page to display it. Browser close-warning behavior.

The energy graph supports selecting retained measured structures and comparing them against a pinned baseline. Frame storage is bounded, so large PDBs may retain fewer structures than energy samples. The final PDB download and Export run records provide coordinates, seeds, hashes, histories and retained frames. Review exported content before sharing. Local benchmark data remains local unless explicitly submitted or shared through another workflow.

docs.title: Appearance and search
docs.text:
Open the palette icon in the upper navigation. Choose Doodle or Observatory, Light/Dark/System, a font, accent and highlight colors, background or local background image. Fresh installations use white Doodle and Simple view. The opening-layout option controls future new tabs; using Dashboard temporarily in one tab does not change the saved choice.

Accent controls charts, progress and interface accents. Highlights independently controls selected dates, active controls, sliders, hover states and text selection. Highlight colors follow the accent until a separate color is chosen. Use accent for highlights restores that link; Reset accent leaves a separately chosen highlight intact. Colors and foreground text adapt to the current theme for contrast, and both preferences are saved across tabs and reloads.

Google search suggestions enables completion while typing. It defaults off. When on, partial queries are sent to Google; submitting a search also opens Google. This option is search completion, not advertisements. Uploaded backgrounds are stored locally; volunteer peers do not receive them.

docs.title: Optional to-do list and doodle board
docs.text:
In the palette menu, under Simple view · personal widgets, enable To-do list or Doodle board and choose Left side, Middle or Right side for each. Both default off, including on upgrades. They appear only in Simple view.

The greeting, search and central widget grid stay centered regardless of which side is occupied. Side tools use the available gutter width and window height; two tools on the same side share that height equally. On narrower windows, side tools move below the main content instead of covering it. Middle uses the compact card format in the central grid, with the same move-earlier/later and resize controls as other widgets.

The arrows and middle-placement icon move a personal widget between these locations. Hover a middle card, or focus it with the keyboard, to reveal its controls. The eye control hides the widget while keeping its contents; enable it again in the palette menu to restore it.

The to-do list supports adding tasks with Enter or +, checking tasks off, deleting individual tasks and Clear completed. The doodle board provides pen colors, an eraser that removes whole strokes, Undo last stroke, movable text notes and a larger editing view. Clear board asks for confirmation before removing drawings and notes. The drawing sheet scrolls vertically, providing additional space in both tall side tools and compact middle cards. Drawings and note proportions are preserved between placements. The board is a bounded scratch space rather than a full infinite-canvas application.

Tasks, strokes and notes save locally in the browser profile and update across its open RoTab tabs. Saving… changes to Saved locally when a write completes; allow it to finish before closing or reloading. Contents are not sent to volunteer peers or included in scientific experiment exports. Clearing extension/site data removes them. There is no cloud synchronization or account requirement.

The controls are shown in an isolated browser profile. Validation summary.

docs.title: Favorites and folders
docs.text:
Hover the favorite bar, or focus its controls with the keyboard, to reveal Add shortcut, Create favorite folder and Configure shortcut rows. Between zero and three rows can be configured. Each row can display favorites, a folder/group or browser most-visited sites. Most-visited rows require optional browser permission. An unavailable or empty list leaves the row empty.

The default Google folder opens nine Google services, with a back tile returning to the main favorites. Folder controls support creating folders, adding existing links, reordering members, removing links and removing a folder while keeping its links. The Google folder uses the same editing and removal controls. Favorite tiles can be edited or deleted directly in Simple view.

The initial favorite row includes the Google folder and bundled science/reading/personal links; the next row defaults to most visited. Favicons keep their proportions inside the tile. Browser-provided site icons or bundled icons are used where available, with initials as fallback.

docs.title: Widgets and calendars
docs.text:
Reveal a widget's upper controls to move it earlier/later, resize it or hide it. The protein tile stays the anchor in Simple view; the remaining tiles reflow on a shared size grid. Dashboard side arrows collapse/reveal the favorites sidebar and the widgets panel to give the protein more space. Computation settings → Restore widgets brings hidden widgets back.

The Calendar gear sits beside its move/resize/hide controls. It opens that calendar's own settings:

Choose Gregorian, Shamsi, Qamari or a combination. One calendar uses a primary calendar grid with compact secondary dates; Separate widgets gives each enabled system its own tile. For a combined grid, choose the primary system. Qamari calculation selects the available civil/Umm al-Qura calculation; regional observation can differ from a computed date.

Use the month arrows to navigate, select a day and use + to add a local event. Local events remain in the browser profile. The Calendar connection icon opens optional Google Calendar setup, which requires a configured OAuth client and separate authorization. Local calendars and events require no Google connection. Privacy and Calendar data.

docs.title: Weather
docs.text:
Weather attempts device location with browser/OS permission and displays the city when resolved, for example Current location - Geneva. If lookup fails or permission is denied, the widget offers city entry. Click the location to change it or retry device location. Each browser profile stores its own choice; there is no preset city.

The smaller weather tile shows available daily details such as wind, humidity, rain chance and sunrise/sunset. Expanding adds the forecast with the selected day range. Unavailable provider fields are omitted. Weather requests go to Open-Meteo and reverse city lookup to Photon/Komoot; this feature is separate from volunteer research.

docs.title: Folding Pomodoro
docs.text:
Click minutes/seconds on the countdown to edit the duration in place. The editor also exposes hours; zero hours are hidden in the normal countdown. Save the duration, then start. Pause retains remaining time; reset restores the configured session duration.

The chain graphic becomes more folded as the timer advances. It is a focus illustration, not a live Rosetta calculation. Completion plays a synthesized ding when the browser permits audio, and a progress ring can appear on the tab icon. Muted tabs, browser audio policy or closing every RoTab can prevent sound. Timer state is separate from submitted proteins and scientific contribution counts.

docs.title: Network is red or a relay rejects the session
docs.text:
Open Volunteer settings → Connection settings → Relay settings and read the exact provider error. Authentication-required, restricted or rate-limited relays are not necessarily usable just because the WebSocket opens. RoTab retries/backoffs per relay and keeps healthy relays/direct links usable. Avoid repeated rapid reconnects. NIP-42 authentication is not implemented; choose a provider that permits this application's rendezvous traffic.

If peers are visible but cannot exchange work, open Live devices. "Waiting for reply" points to the setup exchange; "Reply received" with failed connection checks points to route establishment. Use Retry connections once and allow setup to finish. Update/reload RoTab on both devices so late ICE candidates can be exchanged. Working links and saved jobs/results are retained.

For peers on different networks, successful Nostr discovery does not guarantee a direct WebRTC route. The shared-TURN private pilot includes generated relay access; standard source builds require custom TURN configuration. When connection checks fail, TURN may provide a usable fallback. A slow check or an exchanged reply alone does not prove a firewall restriction. The managed TURN setup guide explains how to obtain credentials, use Test TURN, save settings on both devices and verify a one-model exchange. More Nostr relays cannot replace TURN.

Download connection diagnostics produces a report without candidate IP addresses, raw SDP, participant keys, TURN credentials or scientific payloads. Version 2 includes the built runtime filename and up to four previous connection attempts per peer, so a retry need not erase the earlier failure evidence. Current and previous attempt states can differ. Download from both devices before reloading or changing network settings. Public reports must still exclude private data and any screenshots containing credentials.

docs.title: Shared TURN stops working
docs.text:
Run Test TURN on each device and check whether the configured URL belongs to the current provider tier. Provider quota, authentication expiry, and service availability can affect the shared relay. All shared-pilot users consume one account allowance; a visible Nostr peer can still lack a usable TURN route. See monthly allowance and availability.

When access changes, apply the replacement URL, username and credential on each affected profile, test it and retry connections. An upgrade preserves previously applied TURN settings, so installing a new pilot alone may retain old access. Clearing the URL disables TURN and persists after reload; it does not restore the bundled default. Avoid clearing the browser's identity or campaign ledger to fix relay authentication.

docs.title: Uneven job distribution
docs.text: Check actual connected status, automatic volunteer consent, compatible protocol/engine and whether other sessions are busy or cooling down. One browser profile counts once across its linked tabs. Each network browser accepts one model at a time. A small campaign has only its requested number of independent models, and scheduling is not guaranteed equal-share. The publisher participates only when its campaign's local-participation option is enabled and the session is available.

docs.title: A finished result has not returned
docs.text: Keep/reopen the same publisher profile and its main RoTab. Retained signed outboxes retry over a working direct link. Check whether the publisher is offline, the link failed or the attempt became obsolete through reassignment/cancellation. A lease time passing alone does not discard an otherwise-current result. Clearing either browser's identity/ledger can prevent recovery; relays cannot reconstruct campaign/result data. Export records before deleting local data.

docs.title: Calculation starts, then memory access fails
docs.text:
Pause/stop first, reduce worker count and inspect the exact error. Heap allocation failures and stack/out-of-bounds failures are different issues; more browser cores do not fix either. There is no residue-count cap, but the WASM worker has a 512 MiB linear-memory maximum plus separate compiler/renderer/process overhead. Supported input chemistry/protocol coverage also matters.

The importer uses heap-backed arguments and iterative atom-tree handling. Large designs can still exceed available resources. A minimal authorized input, protocol/seed, browser version and sanitized exported provenance help reproduce a failure. Memory details.

docs.title: Uploaded PDB contains water, ions or ligands
docs.text:
The protein-only importer removes those non-protein components and prunes their LINK/CONECT references. A visible preparation caution identifies the removed components. Review the removed-component details and retain the original PDB. The resulting calculation describes the protein alone, not the original complex.

A modified/nonstandard protein-residue error is different: such residues are retained for review rather than deleted or guessed. Supply a standard-amino-acid structure appropriate to the scientific question. Malformed identifiers, missing backbone coordinates or multiple protein chains also remain explicit errors. Preparation policy and limitations.

docs.title: Long startup or heat while running
docs.text:
Rosetta's first call initializes scientific state and prepares the input before the first measured snapshot. The extension creates a fresh worker per model, so this setup can repeat. Startup is not fully throttled. One worker/10% and the automatic network rest reduce sustained load but do not guarantee temperature/fan behavior. Saved budgets and protocols can differ across devices; cross-device thermal measurements remain pending.

Pause/stop the calculation to end active worker execution. Pause new tasks prevents the next assignment but lets the current one finish. An open extension alone is a different condition from active scientific work. Turning off automatic rotation affects rendering, not the scientific startup path.

docs.title: One or two snapshots, flat graph, or neutral color
docs.text:
Check the method first: Score keeps coordinates fixed and normally emits initial/final snapshots. Minimize/FastRelax can produce an optimization trajectory. Stable starting structures, fast protocols, long operations and the nominal snapshot throttle also affect callback count.

Coordinate storage is bounded to 240 frames and an estimated 8 MiB, so a large target may have fewer retained frames than graph energy samples. Residue-energy coloring requires scored per-residue data in the selected snapshot. A reference structure without that data can appear neutral. Missing intermediate frames cannot be recovered from a final PDB; a new calculation is required to record another trajectory.

docs.title: Weather, Calendar, suggestions or timer sound
docs.text:
Weather: use manual city entry after denied/failed location lookup, and confirm the provider is reachable. Calendar: local events need no account; Google events need a configured OAuth client and authorization. Search suggestions: enable their Appearance checkbox; submitted searches work separately. Timer sound: start via a user action and ensure the tab/browser permits audio; closing all tabs or muting can prevent the ding.

If settings cannot be changed from a linked tab, select Go to main tab. For support, follow the sanitized reporting guide.

docs.title: Connect across networks
docs.text:
Nostr discovery and WebRTC data transfer are separate stages. A peer can appear online before the browsers have a usable route for assignments and results.

Service Role Nostr relay Discover participants and exchange encrypted connection signals STUN Discover candidate network addresses TURN Relay encrypted WebRTC traffic when direct connectivity is unavailable

TURN does not run Rosetta or coordinate campaigns. Scientific transfers use a direct route when one is available.

docs.title: Shared pilot access
docs.text:
The shared-TURN 0.5.2 private pilot includes generated relay access for profiles without an existing TURN configuration. Volunteers do not need separate provider accounts or manual authentication entry. Custom TURN settings and explicit network opt-outs remain saved.

  1. Use compatible RoTab builds and the same room, normally rotab-pilot-v3.
  2. If discovery is disabled, select Join Nostr network in Connection settings.
  3. Select Start volunteering for future compatible work, or Contribute for one offered model.
  4. Check Live devices, then verify assignment, progress, and return of one model.

The submitting browser's main tab coordinates its campaigns and must remain available for assignment and receipts. A volunteer's computing tab must remain open while its model runs.

Shared relay access is readable from the extension build and uses the operator's provider allowance. Expiry, revocation, or quota exhaustion can interrupt fallback connectivity. Custom authentication remains local to the browser profile. The pilot uses the Free-tier standard.relay.metered.ca service over TLS/TCP port 443; the standard source build supplies no shared access.

docs.title: Campaign authority
docs.text:
Any compatible connected participant can submit a target or volunteer. Relay account ownership does not confer an exclusive publishing role. Each sender owns its own campaign ledger, and the room name is a public discovery topic rather than a password.

Also calculate on this browser allows the sender to contribute models through the same queue. Volunteering and submission.

docs.title: Custom TURN settings
docs.text:
A managed service provides TURN without a participant-side server. Custom access requires settings issued by that provider. RoTab is not affiliated with a TURN provider.

In Volunteer settings → Connection settings → Relay settings, enter the issued TURN endpoint and authentication in their respective fields. RoTab currently accepts one TURN URL; a provider's ICE array can list several alternatives. A TLS-over-TCP turns: endpoint on port 443 can be useful on restrictive networks. Provider transport reference.

Select Test TURN on each device. After a successful allocation, select Apply network settings, then Retry connections. A one-model exchange is needed to confirm the complete path between the participants.

Generated relay access is separate from an account password or provider management secret. Provider changes can require updated endpoints and authentication on each affected profile. Previously applied settings are preserved during an extension upgrade. Clearing TURN server and applying the change disables fallback; the empty setting persists after reload.

docs.title: Monthly allowance and availability
docs.text:
Provider information checked October 13, 2026: Metered's Open Relay advertises 20 GB of free TURN traffic each month. The allowance is shared by all devices using one operator account; it is not a separate allowance for each volunteer. Open Relay description.

The provider counts incoming and outgoing relay bytes. Included usage resets each billing period and does not carry over. Free plans can change or be withdrawn and have no service-level or support guarantee. Provider terms, section 7 and Schedule 1.

Quota exhaustion and outages can interrupt relayed transfers while discovery remains visible. Local calculation and working direct routes can continue without TURN. RoTab does not automatically purchase service or provision replacement access.

docs.title: Test results
docs.text:
The illustration uses empty authentication fields in an isolated profile. It shows the controls, not a successful connection between different networks.

Result Meaning TURN relay available This device allocated a relay candidate. Peer connection and job delivery remain separate checks. No relay candidate The endpoint, authentication, provider limits, propagation, or allowed transport need review. Reply received; checking connection Setup is still in progress. Connection checks failed This attempt found no usable route. Waiting for reply The setup exchange has not produced a remote description.

The test creates a temporary relay-only WebRTC connection without a peer or scientific worker. It closes on completion, cancellation, or after twenty seconds. Closing the menu or editing the tested settings cancels it.

docs.title: Diagnostics
docs.text:
Download connection diagnostics records setup state, ICE/transport state, candidate types, numeric server errors, and up to four previous attempts per observed peer. Its in-memory history clears on reconfiguration, peer expiry, or reload.

host identifies a local candidate, srflx an address discovered through STUN, and relay a TURN allocation. A discovered external address does not establish reachability from another network. The report excludes addresses, raw SDP, identities, authentication values, and scientific data. Experiment exports are separate and can contain research data.

docs.title: Validation scope
docs.text: Recorded Chrome and Brave tests established relay allocation and encrypted message/reply transfer over TLS. The shared pilot also returned four WASM minimization models per browser family, with all eight outputs passing independent native rescoring. These tests used isolated profiles on one computer. Different-network reachability and comparative thermal behavior remain unestablished. Benchmark interpretation, connection architecture, validation summaries.

docs.title: Start volunteering
docs.text:
Open the dashboard and select Start volunteering. This enables compatible future assignments under the saved local CPU budget. The standard workflow requires no relay-setting changes. Discovery starts by default; calculation requires explicit volunteering or acceptance of a specific model.

Pause new tasks stops new acceptance while an active model can finish. Contribute on an available campaign accepts one model without opting into all later work. The assigned protein, sender's short description and measured energy/snapshot data appear in the volunteer dashboard.

The Work queue widget summarizes tasks to review, remaining models, observed peers and completed work. Its counts are local observations, not worldwide volunteer totals. A connected green mark is distinct from actual computation/progress. Multiple tabs in one browser profile share one worker owner; different profiles/devices can be separate volunteers.

docs.title: Submit a target
docs.text:
Submission is available to compatible connected participants, including volunteers using the pilot's shared TURN access. It is not restricted to the relay account owner. Each sender coordinates its own campaigns; an approved-sender restriction is not implemented.

Use the paper-plane Publish a target control or the Volunteer network menu. Upload a supported target, choose a fixed method, title, required short research description, number of independent models and starting seed. Keep the description concise: it is limited to 240 characters and shown to volunteers.

The uploader prepares a protein-only copy and shows a caution when water, ions or ligands are removed. Expand its summary to review removals or download the original and prepared files. Volunteers calculate the prepared protein; the excluded components' effects are not included. Modified protein residues are not silently discarded. Input preparation details.

Also calculate on this browser is checked by default, allowing the submitting browser to participate through the same assignment and result-delivery path as remote volunteers. Submit after preparing the target and settings. The submitting browser must remain available to assign work and receive results. Submitted targets are shared with connected volunteers; only authorized research and data may be submitted.

The model count requests independent runs with distinct seeds, not pieces of one large protein. If four models are requested and six eligible devices are present, all six cannot receive one simultaneously. Compatible version, active consent, a working direct connection and availability also affect assignment. The campaign's activity view shows assignment/loading/running, reported energy/progress, stale updates and received results.

Under Your campaigns, click a campaign's title or summary to expand its research description, structure size, seeds, worker activity and scientific provenance. Input files, individual completed models and campaign records are available for download; larger model lists have page controls. Remove requires confirmation before deleting the campaign and its locally saved campaign results and withdrawing new assignments. Models already running may finish, but their late returns are discarded and acknowledged as obsolete. Export required records before removal. Copies in other browsers and separate local run records remain unaffected.

docs.title: Connection settings when needed
docs.text:
Open Volunteer settings → Connection settings. Devices need the same compatible build/wire version and room with reachable relay discovery. Default room is rotab-pilot-v3. Under Relay settings, inspect exact per-relay errors and optionally configure secure relay/STUN/TURN details.

The Live devices illustration uses a controlled six-profile connection fixture. It shows status controls rather than a public volunteer campaign.

Live devices shows whether RoTab is finding a route, waiting for the peer's reply or checking a connection. Retry connections retries disconnected peers while preserving working sessions and saved work. Download connection diagnostics exports setup state and route types without addresses, keys, credentials or protein/job data.

A failed relay is isolated; another healthy relay or existing direct connection may still work. A relay connection cannot guarantee WebRTC reachability. TURN can help restrictive networks. The shared-TURN private pilot installs generated relay access automatically where TURN is absent; volunteers need no provider account or manual credential entry. Custom services can still be configured. Need a TURN service? inside Relay settings provides a managed setup option. Test TURN checks allocation without running science; apply the settings before retrying a peer connection. Follow the cross-network setup guide for steps and test limits. Direct pairing remains an advanced manual invitation/reply alternative.

docs.title: Results and privacy
docs.text:
A worker retains a completed signed result until it gets a matching publisher receipt. If the publisher is offline, delivery can retry when the same session identity/database returns. Received means the matching result was saved, not independently rescored or credited by Rosetta@home. Reassigned/cancelled attempts can make a delayed result obsolete.

Public relays receive presence and encrypted connection signals. Protein files, returned coordinates and descriptions travel directly to connected participants rather than as public Nostr content. Participants can retain data they receive. Read the data and privacy reference, connection architecture and assignment architecture for exact boundaries.

docs.title: Volunteer participation
docs.text: RoTab supports browser-based research calculations using fixed Rosetta protocols. Participation, resource settings, and scientific interpretation have distinct controls and limits.

docs.title: Volunteer consent
docs.text:
Start volunteering authorizes compatible future assignments under the saved local resource budget. Contribute accepts one offered model. Discovery can remain enabled without authorizing computation.

Pause new tasks stops later acceptance while allowing the active model to finish. Pausing or stopping the calculation itself terminates its worker. Completed models remain saved; unfinished models can replay from their recorded seeds. Closing the last RoTab stops browser execution.

Worker count and intensity are local preferences. A publisher cannot raise them remotely. Calculations use CPU, memory, battery, and network bandwidth. Startup is not fully governed by the cooperative intensity target, and temperature/fan behavior varies by device. Completion time and network availability are not guaranteed.

docs.title: Submitted research
docs.text:
A submitted campaign shares its target with assigned participants and can display its title and description in their dashboards. Submission therefore requires authority to share and compute the supplied data. Confidential research and personal information require appropriate handling outside this public volunteer workflow.

The submitting browser coordinates assignments and collects results. Its availability and local database are part of the campaign's recovery boundary. Browser storage is not a permanent research archive; exported records provide a separate copy.

Recipients can retain data delivered to them. Removing a local campaign does not erase copies already received by volunteers. Data and privacy.

docs.title: Scientific interpretation
docs.text:
Energy is reported in Rosetta Energy Units. It is not a clinical measurement or an experimental observation. Optimization snapshots are not a physical molecular-dynamics time series. The Pomodoro chain graphic is a timer illustration and does not run a scientific trajectory.

A signature identifies provenance; a receipt confirms matching delivery. Neither establishes independent scientific correctness. Native rescoring and task-specific validation remain separate from ordinary network admission.

RoTab supplies no diagnosis, treatment recommendation, payment, cryptocurrency mining, official Rosetta@home result acceptance, or BOINC credit. The project is independent of endorsement by RosettaCommons, Rosetta@home, and BOINC.

docs.title: Services and rights
docs.text: Rosetta, its database, and third-party services have terms separate from original RoTab application code. Licensing and availability describes the component boundaries. Relay, STUN/TURN, weather, and Google services retain their own availability and data practices.

docs.title: Data and privacy
docs.text: This reference describes the data handled by RoTab 0.5.6. It explains browser storage, network recipients, optional services, and deletion behavior. It is a technical description, not an operator-specific legal privacy notice.

docs.title: Data handling
docs.text:
Information Purpose Storage and recipients Appearance, preferred layout, favorites, widget order, timer, and local events Personalize the new-tab page Browser-profile storage Optional most-visited site list Populate frequent-site shortcuts Read through the browser's optional topSites permission and displayed locally Search text Submit a Google search Sent to Google on submission; optional suggestions also send partial queries while typing City or device coordinates Obtain weather and a location label Stored locally; forecast/geocoding requests go to Open-Meteo and approximate device coordinates to Photon/Komoot Imported structures, prepared inputs, protocol, seeds, coordinates, and energies Local calculations and submitted campaigns Local IndexedDB; submitted or accepted network work transfers relevant scientific data to participant browsers Public participant identity, capability, availability, and bounded counts Discover compatible volunteers Public Nostr presence and connected peers Encrypted signaling and ICE metadata Establish WebRTC connections Selected relays, peers, and STUN/TURN services Signing identities and connection authentication Authenticate sessions and relay access Browser-profile storage; shared pilot relay access is included in its extension build Optional Google Calendar events and access token Display and edit the selected calendar Google Calendar API; the token is retained in browser-session storage To-do tasks, doodle strokes, and board notes Personal Simple-view tools Local IndexedDB, shared only with RoTab tabs in the same browser profile Worker memory, progress, elapsed time, and optional energy Display resource use and calculation status Local UI; an assigned worker also reports bounded progress directly to its publisher

RoTab has no developer analytics endpoint, advertising integration, or sale of personal information. External services apply their own data practices to requests they receive.

docs.title: Discovery and scientific sharing
docs.text:
Discovery is enabled by default while a coordinating RoTab session is open. It announces a persistent pseudonymous public identity, room topic, capabilities, and bounded availability metadata to the selected Nostr relays. Calculation requires Start volunteering or acceptance of a specific model. Connection settings can disable discovery.

The default discovery relays are wss://relay.damus.io and wss://nos.lol. Relays receive public presence and encrypted signaling. Protein files, returned structures, and research descriptions are transferred over WebRTC rather than published as plaintext relay events. A room name is a discovery topic, not a private access-control secret.

Connected participants receive campaign descriptions; assigned workers receive their targets. Publishers receive signed outputs and progress. Recipients can retain or export scientific content they receive. Transport encryption does not prevent an authorized recipient from copying a structure or establish the correctness of a result.

STUN/TURN services receive connectivity metadata and any authentication required for relay allocation. TURN relays carry encrypted WebRTC traffic when direct connectivity is unavailable. The shared pilot includes generated relay access, which can be extracted from the extension; it does not include the provider account password or account-management API secret. Custom connection settings remain local. Test TURN checks allocation without transferring a scientific input or starting a calculation.

docs.title: Optional services
docs.text:
Weather uses a manually entered city or device location with browser/OS permission. Device coordinates are rounded to two decimal places before the city-name lookup. Location is not published to volunteers. Failed or declined detection offers city entry.

Google search suggestions default off. Enabling them sends partial queries to Google; submitting a search opens Google independently of that preference. Most-visited shortcuts require optional browser permission.

Google Calendar requires optional access, authorization, and a configured OAuth client. Calendar data is used for the displayed calendar and requested event operations. It is not sent to volunteer peers or scientific exports and is not used by RoTab for advertising.

An explicitly configured hosted research API is a separate optional mode. It receives task/result data and protocol identifiers. The default browser build has no hosted research API origin.

docs.title: Local retention and deletion
docs.text:
Preferences and identities remain until changed or browser data is removed. The latest 20 completed browser run records are retained. Each model's display history is bounded to 2,000 energy samples and up to 240 coordinate frames within an estimated 8 MiB frame budget. Campaign records, imported inputs, and pending signed results remain until removed or browser storage is cleared or evicted.

Removing a campaign deletes its local input, attempts, and outcomes and withdraws future assignments. Up to 128 recent worker identifiers may remain as connection hints for acknowledging late returns. These hints contain no deleted protein coordinates or results. Separate browser run records and copies held by other participants remain independent.

Favorites, tasks, board contents, and local events have deletion controls. Clearing extension data removes the broader local stores. Downloaded exports and browser backups can remain separately. RoTab cannot erase another participant's copy or a service provider's logs.

Disconnecting Google Calendar removes RoTab's local token. It does not delete Google events or necessarily revoke authorization in the Google account. Disabling discovery stops future rendezvous activity but does not recall information already received by relays or peers.

docs.title: Security boundaries
docs.text:
Executable JavaScript and WASM are packaged with the extension. Network jobs select supported protocols and cannot supply executable code. Signed messages and encrypted signaling authenticate transfer paths; they do not provide independent scientific validation.

Profile storage is not protected by an additional application-level encryption layer or a claim of hardware-backed key storage. Access to the browser profile can expose its records and authentication material. Experiment exports omit signing secrets, OAuth tokens, and TURN authentication, but can contain complete structures, descriptions, and participant identifiers.

docs.title: Documentation website
docs.text:
The documentation is hosted through GitHub Pages. Requests can disclose ordinary web metadata, including IP address and browser details, to GitHub under its privacy statement. The site uses local system fonts and contains no RoTab advertising or analytics integration.

Help and security describes troubleshooting and the information appropriate for a public issue.

docs.title: Help and security
docs.text: The illustrated Help guide covers controls and ordinary workflows. Troubleshooting explains connection failures, missing results, snapshots, and memory use.

docs.title: Problem reports
docs.text:
A useful report identifies the extension version, browser and operating system, calculation protocol, resource settings, and steps that reproduce the problem. The stage of failure also matters: connection, engine startup, calculation, or result delivery.

Live devices → Download connection diagnostics exports route types and setup state without candidate addresses, raw SDP, authentication values, participant identities, or scientific payloads. This is separate from an experiment export.

A scientific report can include an authorized minimal structure, seed, method, and provenance. Experiment exports can contain complete structures and research descriptions. Public issues are suitable only for information authorized for disclosure.

The documentation repository provides a reference point for readers with repository access. No private security-reporting address is listed in this documentation. Passwords, access tokens, signing keys, browser profiles, and confidential datasets should not be posted publicly.

docs.title: Security boundaries
docs.text: Potential security problems include exposed authentication material, signature/admission bypass, acceptance of executable job content, or cross-origin data leakage. RoTab does not provide remote key recovery or deletion of another participant's copies. No security-audit certification or guaranteed response time is represented here.

docs.title: Local data controls
docs.text:
Favorites, tasks, board contents, and local events can be removed through their editors. Browser extension-data controls remove the broader profile-local stores. Required scientific records should be exported before deletion.

Disconnecting Google Calendar discards RoTab's local session token. Google account authorization and existing Google events remain separate. The data reference describes retention and recipients.

docs.title: API and lifecycle
docs.text: All public declarations are generated under packages/rosetta-wasm/dist/. The root import exports the client, methods, input utilities, protocol IDs, engine/source constants and typed events/results. Individual method subpaths are listed in the catalogue.

docs.title: Client construction and execution
docs.text:
const client = createRosetta({
  engineUrl: "/science/engine/",
  workerUrl: "/science/sdk/worker.js", // optional when default relative worker remains intact
});
const result = await client.run("minimize", pdb, options);
client.close();

engineUrl is a directory URL without query or fragment. It contains the four required engine files. One client owns one reusable dedicated worker. Construction does not calculate; run validates the request before creating its worker. Concurrent calls on the same client reject as busy. After a successful result, the next call reuses the module and resets the RNG seed. Separate clients are independent workers with independent memory.

The SDK checks the exact measured manifest, source and eight-protocol catalogue, then hashes the JS glue, WASM and database before instantiation. Verified WASM/database bytes are passed to the factory. JavaScript is imported from the trusted static URL after checking it; use immutable/versioned hosting. Pin checks detect mixed or corrupted deployments but cannot attest an untrusted browser or a hostile server that changes its response between checking and importing.

docs.title: RunOptions
docs.text:
Field Contract seed Integer from 1 to 2,000,000,000; default 17 dutyCycle Integer from 10 to 75; default 25; cooperative per-worker active-time target signal AbortSignal; abort terminates the worker and rejects with AbortError onPhase verifying-assets, loading-module, calculating onSnapshot Actual structure/REF2015 state callback onLog Optional Rosetta/runtime diagnostic strings; not structured scientific output

Observer callback exceptions are logged and do not strand the scientific promise. There is no timer-enforced scientific deadline in the client; a caller can use an AbortController and its own watchdog. No arbitrary score weights, repeat counts, scripts, command-line flags or movers are accepted.

docs.title: StructureSnapshot
docs.text:
Field Meaning pdb, energy Actual intermediate structure and common REF2015 energy in REU source initial, stage, minimizing, packing, final sequence Per-call callback sequence, reset for each run iteration Source callback counter; not guaranteed to be an accepted optimizer step progress Stage estimate; some methods stay at zero until final; not time remaining timestamp Wall-clock callback timestamp, milliseconds heapBytes Allocated WASM linear memory at callback time; excludes process/compiler/viewer overhead

Callback rate is scientific-state dependent, with a nominal internal 200 ms throttle. A final snapshot can arrive before final host hashing/validation resolves the Promise. Retain frame IDs together with a run/model identity if combining trajectories.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
pdb, energy, protocol, scoreFunction, sequence are the scientific output. energy is REF2015 evaluation of the returned PDB-rounded coordinates. objectiveEnergy and objectiveScoreFunction describe the optimization objective before serialization. Cartesian methods use ref2015_cart; all reported final energies use ref2015.

activeMs, sleepingMs, yields, liveSnapshots, minimizerEvaluations and packingMoves are harness diagnostics. They are not OS CPU time, physical time or counts of scientifically independent samples. Their accounting omits some unyielded trailing work and does not replace a controlled performance experiment.

provenance records engine/source IDs, the three measured file hashes, input/output SHA-256, seed and duty target. It identifies bytes and settings; it does not cryptographically prove execution or native equivalence.

Timing field Scope initializationMs Cold SDK asset download/checking plus Emscripten factory; zero when reusing a loaded worker calculationMs The C ABI call, including lazy scientific initialization on the first call totalMs Worker-side request through final validation/hash preparation; excludes caller render/download/network delivery

docs.title: Abort, close and restart
docs.text:
Abort terminates the current worker. The client may start a fresh worker on a later run, but unfinished scientific state is lost. Calling close() releases its worker, aborts pending work and permanently closes the client. Create another client for further work.

The standalone SDK does not implement pause/checkpoint/recovery or choose half the cores automatically. Its caller schedules separate seeded runs and persists completed outputs. RoTab's Session supplies those product behaviors above the same C ABI. Replaying an unfinished seed is not a resume from the last displayed PDB.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Invalid inputs, unknown protocols, seed/intensity bounds, changed manifests, corrupted assets, load/runtime failures and invalid result contracts reject the run. A worker error terminates that worker before another attempt. Resource exhaustion is possible even for an admitted PDB because finite browser/compiler/heap memory remains. No method silently falls back to a different calculation.

docs.title: Low-level C ABI
docs.text:
const char* rosettatab_run_protocol(
    const char* pdb, const char* protocol, int seed, int duty_percent);

Allocate the PDB as a null-terminated UTF-8 buffer on the WASM heap, then use Emscripten ccall with return type string, argument types ["number", "string", "number", "number"], values [pdbPointer, protocol, seed, duty] and { async: true }. Keep the buffer allocated until the asynchronous call settles, and release it in finally. Read the current HEAPU8 after allocation because memory growth replaces its view.

ccall string conversion places the complete argument on the C stack, which is only 1 MiB in this build. Large PDBs require the heap-buffer path. The extension and standalone worker share packages/shared/src/wasm-bridge.ts; both capture the pinned binary's existing malloc/free exports through the supported instantiateWasm hook. Emscripten string and pointer arguments.

Parse the returned JSON and reject its error field. The returned C string points to a harness-owned static response; copy/parse it before another call. The ABI permits only one active invocation per module. rosettatab_run(pdb, relaxFlag, seed, duty) remains only for older pilot compatibility. The SDK exposes the safe worker host rather than requiring consumers to manage globals manually.

docs.title: Build and validation reference
docs.text: This chapter describes source builds and validation. Participants use packaged browser assets; rebuilding the scientific engine is optional. The coordinate port, standalone SDK and documentation require no Docker or task server.

docs.title: Scientific prerequisites
docs.text:
Rebuilding requires an authorized Rosetta source checkout, Git, Python, CMake, a native C++ toolchain and the pinned Emscripten SDK. Repository scripts fetch and build the source and dependencies, which can require substantial storage and build time. Existing verified artifacts can be reused for private SDK development after hash verification.

npm run engine:fetch
ROSETTATAB_WITH_RELAX=ON npm run engine:configure
ROSETTATAB_WITH_RELAX=ON ROSETTATAB_BUILD_MODE=native npm run engine:build
ROSETTATAB_WITH_RELAX=ON ROSETTATAB_BUILD_MODE=wasm npm run engine:build

The historical WITH_RELAX option name enables the complete current coordinate protocol set, including design/minimization. ROSETTATAB_JOBS controls compiler parallelism. Build-time concurrency is separate from scientific browser worker count. ROSETTATAB_DATABASE can choose a candidate database path; use the proven reduced database for matching existing artifacts.

docs.title: Reduced database preparation
docs.text:
The full upstream database is much larger than the measured browser package. Candidate resources are selected from actual successful native reads using ROSETTATAB_TRACE_DATABASE=1 and scripts/package-database.py.

mkdir -p build
ROSETTATAB_TRACE_DATABASE=1 engine/artifacts/native/rosettatab-native \
  --input apps/extension/public/fixtures/1l2y.pdb \
  --database .vendor/rosetta/database --protocol relax --seed 17 \
  2> build/database-trace.log
python3 scripts/package-database.py build/database-trace.log

This single example creates only a candidate for its exercised reads. It is insufficient to reconstruct the current expanded 908-resource catalogue by itself or certify the eight protocols. A validated database requires traces from the intended chemistry/protocol fixtures, a resource manifest, and corresponding native/browser checks. A new database changes rosetta.data and invalidates old exact-build evidence.

docs.title: Scientific and browser gates
docs.text:
npm run engine:verify-protocols
npm run build
npm run engine:verify-browser
npm run engine:verify-browser-protocols
npm run engine:verify-browser-protocols -- --brave
npm run engine:verify-inputs
npm run engine:package

Native/Node protocol checks compare all eight methods and rescore outputs. Installed Chrome/Brave checks exercise normal VMs, live callbacks and matching assets. Recovery/input checks are separate. engine:package refuses changed or unverified builds and writes engine/artifacts/verified. This is the scientific payload used by the extension and standalone bundle.

docs.title: Standalone adapter
docs.text:
npm run sdk:build
npm run sdk:pack
npm run sdk:bundle
npm run sdk:verify-browser

The first command bundles original adapter/input-validation code with esbuild and emits declarations through TypeScript. It does not recompile or modify Rosetta. sdk:pack produces a local npm tarball; sdk:bundle makes the private static example with pinned science assets. sdk:verify-browser runs real score/minimize/relax through the standalone API in Chrome and Brave and independently rescores the outputs using the developer native reference.

The SDK browser verifier requires an existing static development preview at 127.0.0.1:5173 to stream the 117 MB WASM asset. The verifier does not launch that preview; other static fixtures use Playwright interception. No extension is loaded, all external requests are blocked, and records distinguish this three-method SDK smoke test from the engine's eight-protocol validation. Calculation does not contact a task API or native program; independent native rescoring is a separate validation step.

docs.title: Research application modules
docs.text:
The coordinate SDK exposes eight methods with fixed settings. Two additional research WASM targets under engine/artifacts/wasm provide broader scientific dispatch and cyclic peptide experiments. Both remain outside the extension and supported SDK.
