docs.title: Cyclic evidence and unresolved issue
docs.text:
The smaller cyclic family produced one eight-residue fixture containing two D-residues. Its stored energy 10.319999695 REU agreed with native silent-record rescoring 10.319698257 within 0.001 REU. Topology checks found the N-to-C ring bond, a 1.328840518 Å closure distance and two D-amino-acid residue types. Recorded heap was 231,997,440 bytes. This is one Node WASM fixture, not general cyclic validation.

Silent records preserve annotated chemical topology. Converting a cyclic/D-residue record to an ordinary linear canonical PDB and rescoring would test a different molecule. A separate native control's first silent record failed score agreement on reimport (9.826 versus 55.383 REU); that unresolved result remains in the evidence and blocks a general silent-format compatibility claim. The returned WASM cyclic fixtures passed their own independent rescoring.

docs.title: Browser availability
docs.text: These modules have no supported participant browser API and are unavailable through client.run. A supported family requires a fixed input schema, validated resources, a browser host, measured snapshots, and output/topology validation.

docs.title: Standalone deployment and integration
docs.text: The SDK is a browser library independent of Chrome permissions, Nostr, job scheduling, React, backend databases and native companions. The host application provides its UI, consent controls, persistence and any transport of scientific inputs and results. Quick start covers package imports; this chapter specifies deployment requirements and worker lifetime.

docs.title: Static file contract
docs.text:
public/science/
  sdk/                       # copy the entire generated dist, not just index.js
    index.js, worker.js, chunks…, methods/…, *.d.ts
  engine/
    manifest.json
    rosetta.mjs
    rosetta.wasm
    rosetta.data
    licensing and citation files

Use a versioned directory on static HTTPS hosting. Supply that engine directory and the SDK worker URL to createRosetta. Keep worker dependencies/chunks together. Serve JavaScript as JavaScript, .wasm as application/wasm and .data as binary. A single-page-app fallback must not return index.html for a missing scientific file. Opening file:// is not a supported module/fetch deployment.

The worker must be served from the application's origin. Cross-origin engine assets require CORS authorization for that origin and permission in the application's Content Security Policy (CSP). Relevant directives may include script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval', worker-src 'self' and a suitable connect-src for asset fetches. These fragments must be integrated into the site's complete policy. The current single-threaded build does not require pthreads, SharedArrayBuffer or COOP/COEP.

For a Chrome extension, bundle executable JS/WASM in the extension package. Do not copy a website's remote-executable-asset deployment into Manifest V3. Chrome's remote hosted code guidance.

docs.title: Client lifecycle
docs.text:
import { createRosetta, preparePdb } from "@rotab/rosetta-wasm";

const client = createRosetta({
  engineUrl: new URL("/science/engine/", location.href),
  workerUrl: new URL("/science/sdk/worker.js", location.href),
});
const controller = new AbortController();
const prepared = preparePdb(originalPdb);

try {
  const common = { seed: 17, dutyCycle: 10, signal: controller.signal };
  const initial = await client.score(prepared.pdb, common);
  const refined = await client.minimize(prepared.pdb, {
    ...common,
    onSnapshot: frame => recordMeasuredFrame(frame),
  });
  await saveLocally({ originalPdb, preparation: prepared.report, initial, refined });
} finally {
  client.close();
}
// A Stop control can call controller.abort() during an active call.

originalPdb, recordMeasuredFrame and saveLocally are supplied by the host application. Both runs in this example use the prepared original input. Chaining returned coordinates requires explicitly passing initial.pdb to the next call. Sequential calls reuse the client's initialized scientific state. Concurrent calls on one client are rejected; separate clients allocate separate heaps. One client is the recommended initial configuration, with parallelism selected only after resource assessment.

Abort terminates the worker and rejects with AbortError. A later run on the still-open client starts a fresh worker and repeats setup. close() permanently closes that client. Neither operation serializes unfinished Rosetta state. The host application is responsible for persisting completed outputs and seeds before starting another model.

docs.title: Asset verification and trust
docs.text:
The worker checks the manifest and all three scientific SHA-256 pins before instantiating the WASM module. It compiles verified WASM bytes, supplies them through instantiateWasm, and mounts verified database bytes through getPreloadedPackage. A changed engine/database needs deliberate pin updates and new matching scientific gates; disabling verification is not an integration fix.

The worker checks the fetched bytes of rosetta.mjs before importing it from the configured trusted static origin. A hash check cannot attest a hostile host or browser or prevent a server from changing the later import response. Deployment requires immutable, versioned assets from a controlled origin, with production-host checks for MIME types, CORS, CSP and error handling.

docs.title: Records and rendering
docs.text:
onSnapshot provides actual PDB coordinates, REF2015 energy (REU), source/counter/progress, timestamp and allocated heap bytes. Feed PDBs to a viewer such as Mol*, but retain measured values before any interpolation/downsampling. Score normally produces initial/final snapshots of the same coordinates; Minimize/FastRelax can provide a changing optimization trajectory. Callback counts are not a molecular-dynamics time axis.

Final results include output PDB, protocol, sequence, reported REF2015 score, distinct optimization objective, input/output hashes, source/engine identity, seed/intensity and timing scopes. timing.initializationMs covers asset checks/factory startup; lazy Rosetta setup on the first call belongs to calculationMs. Cooperative activeMs/sleepingMs omit initialization before the timer is enabled and are not hardware CPU/temperature readings.

Persistence and network delivery are responsibilities of the host application. The SDK does not save IndexedDB records, upload to a project or award BOINC credit. Integration and distribution requirements include the input/output contracts, memory limitations, benchmark scope and licensing conditions.

docs.title: Deployment verification
docs.text: Deployment validation covers root and method imports, relative worker chunks, downloaded asset hashes, cold/warm Score and Minimize, cancellation, repeated sequential calls and offline/missing-file errors. Records identify the browser/version, input/seed, timing scope and memory availability. Intended larger inputs require separate testing because browser memory remains finite despite the absence of a residue-count cap. Private fixtures and native rescoring establish only their recorded scientific scope.

docs.title: Strict coordinate input
docs.text:
The admitted methods take PDB text representing one nonempty protein chain of the 20 standard amino-acid types. Every residue needs N, CA, C and O backbone atoms. Coordinates must be finite and within the existing admission range of ±10,000 Å. Duplicate atoms, unresolved alternate-location labels, multiple coordinate models, HETATM chemistry and conflicting residue names are rejected by strict validation.

Input validation imposes no residue-count cap. Execution remains constrained by the 512 MiB per-worker heap ceiling, browser compiler/process memory and reduced database coverage. A large input may pass admission and still fail during calculation. Structure-record validation does not comprehensively detect missing biological segments, unusual covalent topology or every malformed PDB convention.

Full PDB arguments use a heap buffer rather than the small C stack. Browser-specific atom-tree traversal and release also use heap worklists to avoid deep call-stack failures. See large protein memory for the adaptations, regression checks and remaining resource limits.

Use validatePdb(pdb) for admission without preparation. It returns { residues, atoms, chain }. Supported standalone text input is PDB, not a general mmCIF/FASTA/fragments/silent-file API. The extension can unpack certain local file containers before applying the same coordinate policy; that capability is not implicitly part of the standalone method ABI.

docs.title: Explicit preparation
docs.text:
preparePdb(original) creates a protein-only copy, validates the prepared result, and returns { pdb, changed, report }. Preparation is explicit in the standalone SDK and automatic for extension uploads. Keep the original bytes and report together with the calculation record.

Situation Preparation action BOM / Windows line endings Normalize text and record the change Multiple MODEL records Select the first complete coordinate model and record selection Alternate atom locations Choose one complete backbone conformer per residue, ranked by mean valid occupancy; A wins ties Identical duplicate atom records Remove exact duplicates and count them Conflicting duplicates Reject instead of guessing Crystallographic HOH/WAT/DOD, including linked water Remove for this implicit-solvent protocol and count atoms Non-protein HETATM ions and ligands Exclude from the protein-only copy; report component names, residue counts and atom counts LINK/CONECT references to excluded components Remove the LINK record or excluded CONECT target; preserve protein-to-protein connectivity Standard amino acids recorded as HETATM Retain coordinates and normalize the record type to ATOM Modified/noncanonical protein residues Reject rather than delete or substitute a protein residue Extra protein chains or missing backbone Retain/reject; never select a chain silently or fabricate coordinates

Conformer selection does not choose each atom independently. Shared blank-location atoms can accompany the selected conformer. Removing alternate models/conformers or waters changes the input representation and must be reported. A prepared file's SHA-256 differs from the original when its bytes change.

The current report policy is pdb-protein-only-preparation-v2. It includes nonProteinRemoved entries with name, kind, residues and atoms, plus counts for removed LINK records, removed CONECT references and canonical HETATM records converted to ATOM. The existing waterAtomsRemoved count remains available. Saved v1 reports remain readable. Use the updated build on participants receiving prepared campaigns so that the v2 original-input provenance is recognized.

The extension displays an always-visible caution before calculation or submission, with expandable details and Original PDB / Prepared PDB downloads. Originals and both hashes are retained in local calculation provenance. The SDK caller must provide its own notice and retain the original; preparePdb does not overwrite a file or keep a separate archive.

Removing a metal, ligand, cofactor or linked water changes the modeled system. Results apply to the retained protein, with those components and their interactions excluded. This workflow does not reproduce the energy of the original complex or automatically repair covalent adducts. Modified protein residues declared by MODRES, common unsupported amino acids and protein-like HETATM backbones are rejected conservatively; incomplete or unusual chemistry can still need manual preparation. Standard-atom coordinates remain unchanged by component removal, but the complete scientific system is different.

Connectivity pruning follows the fixed-width endpoints in the wwPDB LINK format. Component cleanup is input preparation, not added Rosetta ligand or metal support.

docs.title: Output identity
docs.text:
Every method returns a PDB and the computed sequence. All eight preserve residue count and PDB residue identifiers in the admitted fixture contract. Non-design methods must also preserve residue names. fixed_backbone_design and fastdesign may change canonical residue identities; they are not safe substitutions when the scientific intent requires an unchanged sequence.

The host validates returned PDB syntax, residue identity and reported objective/energy types. These checks do not replace independent scientific rescoring or confirm all topology/geometry. Native acceptance tools rescore returned coordinates and compare with the tolerance defined in benchmarks.

docs.title: Energies and rounding
docs.text:
The C++ harness serializes coordinates to PDB, reimports those rounded coordinates, then computes the returned energy with full-weight REF2015. objectiveEnergy is evaluated on the pre-serialization pose. Cartesian objectives additionally change two weights; their values must not be directly mixed with common REF2015 history.

Intermediate display snapshots score a pose copy before PDB serialization. Reimporting the snapshot's rounded PDB can yield a slightly different value. Final Result.energy explicitly uses returned-coordinate rescoring. Preserve this distinction when comparing snapshot, pose-table, score-file and final-coordinate energies.

Rosetta Energy Units are objective values, not watts or physical time. Lower energy is a protocol-specific ranking signal, not proof that a designed sequence folds, is experimentally stable or has a particular function.

docs.title: Records for reuse or publication
docs.text:
Store the original file, prepared input/report, SHA-256 of both, protocol, seed, fixed work budget, complete result, output hash, engine/source/data hashes, browser/OS versions, timing scope and errors. If retaining frames, record which samples were dropped and which model owns each frame. Keep failed runs in the experimental record rather than reporting only successes.

The SDK's result provenance covers its exact prepared input and returned output. It does not automatically retain originals, browser versions, full history, experiment IDs, campaign/participant IDs or independent validation. Its caller owns those records; RoTab's Session/export formats add those product-level fields.

docs.title: Large protein memory handling
docs.text: Memory regression testing includes an authorized private structure with 865 residues, 14,263 atom records, and 1,155,392 UTF-8 bytes. The calculation retains its protein coordinates without splitting the chain or imposing a residue-count cap. The structure and raw records are not distributed with this documentation.

docs.title: Stack and heap boundaries
docs.text:
Emscripten's ccall string conversion uses the C stack. The measured build has a 1 MiB stack, so a large PDB can exhaust it before scientific execution even when linear-memory usage remains below the 512 MiB heap ceiling.

The extension and SDK use packages/shared/src/wasm-bridge.ts to allocate a null-terminated UTF-8 input on the WASM heap. The bridge passes a numeric pointer, retains the allocation across asynchronous yields, and releases it after the call. It reads the current HEAPU8 after allocation because memory growth replaces the typed-array view. Allocation failures are reported before Rosetta is entered. Emscripten argument lifetime.

docs.title: Atom-tree adaptations
docs.text:
Deep atom trees can also exceed Chromium's execution stack. The WASM build excludes synchronous core::kinematics::tree::* routines from Asyncify instrumentation because they cannot reach the scientific pause or snapshot hooks.

Two WASM-specific adaptations use heap worklists:

Operation Preserved behavior Domain-map traversal Depth-first child order, local color state, sibling color propagation, and domain assignments Atom-tree release Child ownership during cleanup and externally retained subtrees

The native comparison retains the original recursive implementations. A native test host compared the exact iterative bodies against the recursive reference across 100 deterministic movement-mask combinations. It also checked release of unretained atoms and preservation of an externally held root's subtree. These checks passed for 20-residue 1L2Y and the larger structure, which produced 14,300 tree atoms.

The scientific ABI, score function, protocol budgets, and input-preparation policy are unchanged by these memory adaptations.

docs.title: Large-input validation
docs.text:
The complete 865-residue Score calculation passed in installed Chrome and Brave. The standalone SDK also processed that input after its score/minimize/relax checks. Its recorded warm WASM heap was 278,396,928 bytes (265.5 MiB).

Measurement Result WASM returned-coordinate energy −1592.9555612337726 REU Independent native returned-coordinate score −1592.9555612336503 REU Per-worker linear-memory ceiling 512 MiB

The large-input checks verified residue retention, original/prepared input provenance, and independent native rescoring. Raw private structures are excluded from the public records. Success with Score does not establish FastRelax, repacking, or sequence-design support for the same large input; packing can require substantially more memory.

Most eight-method scientific checks use 20-residue 1L2Y. The documented FastDesign fixture uses eight residues. The historical full 20-residue FastDesign result belongs to a different engine build. Benchmark scope.

docs.title: Parallel startup
docs.text:
A single-worker run compiles WASM inside its disposable worker. Concurrent extension pools compile one immutable WebAssembly.Module and share it through structured cloning. Each worker still owns its own instance, linear memory, filesystem, Rosetta globals, and RNG. The module is not a checkpoint and is not sent over the volunteer network. Sharing compiled modules.

Shared compilation alone did not prevent a renderer crash during six simultaneous cold Rosetta initializations. Startup is therefore staged: the next worker begins after an earlier instance emits its first scientific frame. Initialized calculations can continue concurrently up to the configured worker limit.

A six-model Brave Score check retained all six outputs with one WASM fetch and no page errors. Its observed aggregate allocated heap peaked at 412,614,656 bytes (393.5 MiB) during staged startup. This was not a measurement of six fully initialized workers or total browser RAM. The corresponding Chrome observation did not complete the same six-output verification.

docs.title: Completion and retained memory
docs.text:
Completion terminates the scientific worker and clears its message/error handlers. The pool releases transient live data and its shared compiled-module reference when no further launch requires them. Saved PDBs, energy histories, and bounded coordinate frames remain available for replay and export.

The recovery path reads saved trajectories only when an incoming assignment needs a result recovered. An idle or fully delivered dashboard does not repeatedly deserialize all 20 retained runs.

WASM heap measures worker linear memory. UI JS heap estimates JavaScript allocation for the viewing page. Neither measures the complete browser tab, compiled code, renderer, GPU, or process overhead. Browser caching and garbage collection can delay reclamation after workers end. Chrome memory measurement scopes.

docs.title: Recorded completion observations
docs.text:
Chrome 153 checks on October 12, 2026 sampled the largest renderer process after 30 seconds of natural idle. The measurements did not depend on forced garbage collection.

Condition Renderer RSS after idle Bundled single-worker FastRelax before the lifecycle change Approximately 524 MiB Bundled single-worker FastRelax after the lifecycle change Approximately 185 MiB First of two sequential Score runs on the private 865-residue input Approximately 493 MiB Second Score run on that input Approximately 346 MiB Two-worker 1L2Y Score Approximately 281 MiB

The FastRelax runs used different seeds and were not a controlled matched-seed benchmark. Both used the same scientific engine and 75% diagnostic intensity, which differs from participant defaults.

The two large-input Score runs produced identical output hashes and energies. Both workers terminated, and their results and initial/final frames remained saved. The two-worker 1L2Y check likewise retained both seeded outputs and terminated both workers after one shared compilation.

These observations did not reproduce persistent 1.5 GB retention. They do not establish a universal memory ceiling or reproduce a user's existing browser profile. Operating-system RSS also differs from Chrome's tab-hover attribution.

docs.title: Rosetta C++ to WebAssembly architecture
docs.text: The port compiles Rosetta's C++ scientific implementations for execution in browser workers. Platform adaptations provide browser-compatible builds, resource loading, cooperative scheduling and measured snapshots. The production coordinate API uses a harness with fixed protocol settings; it does not expose the unrestricted native command-line application.

docs.title: 1. Source pinning and build assembly
docs.text:
scripts/fetch-engine.sh checks out Rosetta commit 369e400415dd5c585f80dcf7b647147ee520e8ba, initializes selected upstream submodules and activates Emscripten 6.0.11. scripts/prepare-engine.py checks the source HEAD, generates Rosetta options/type definitions and constructs CMake source lists from upstream project manifests.

Core/utility/scoring code is always included; ROSETTATAB_WITH_RELAX=ON adds the protocol libraries needed by all eight methods. Applications are not all linked into the bounded coordinate target. CUDA translation units are excluded. Native and WASM reference targets use the same harness and pinned scientific source; the build also applies the documented portability patches.

docs.title: 2. Platform adaptations
docs.text:
Adaptation Reason Scientific effect Emscripten/Linux platform headers and definitions Browser target has no native macOS/Windows ABI Platform compilation, not energy formula replacement POSIX backtrace guard execinfo diagnostics are unavailable Diagnostic fallback only Bundled SQLite header; static dependencies Avoid host-specific database/backend/linker dependencies No task-server dependency in participant Disable thread/shared-object/plugin loading paths Current worker is a single CPU WASM instance No native plugins, process/MPI/pthread execution Merge split Boost headers Portable header layout Build adaptation Bounded energy-method registration Avoid linking unrelated creators into browser startup Limits supported score/chemistry surface; not arbitrary Rosetta support Traced database reads Identify files used by admitted fixtures Reduced resources need validation; a trace is not universal coverage Heap-backed PDB arguments ccall's temporary string uses the 1 MiB C stack Same complete input bytes; buffer retained across asynchronous yields Iterative atom-tree release in WASM Avoid a recursive shared-pointer cleanup cascade exceeding the browser stack Ownership cleanup only; retained subtrees and scientific state are preserved; native reference unchanged Iterative domain-map traversal in WASM Deep recursive traversal can exceed Chromium's baseline VM stack Preserve depth-first child order, sibling color propagation and domain assignments; native reference unchanged

The registration list is engine/ref2015-creators.txt. Native reference registration remains complete; the WASM registry retains the supported REF2015-related creators. Excluded methods are unavailable through this host, with no substitute approximation.

docs.title: 3. Scientific ABI
docs.text:
engine/rosettatab.cc imports the PDB into an upstream Pose, constructs REF2015, resets the RNG to the requested seed and selects one allowlisted protocol. It calls upstream FastRelax, MinMover, PackRotamersMover or FastDesign, with the exact bounded settings documented per method. The final output includes sequence, rounded-coordinate REF2015 energy and separately identified objective energy.

Initialization uses explicit database path, constant seed and non-binary Dunbrack loading options. Rosetta's global options are initialized once per worker. Each subsequent coordinate call resets the RNG seed. No remote RosettaScripts, command strings, arbitrary score functions or executable modules enter this interface.

docs.title: 4. Browser asset package
docs.text:
engine/CMakeLists.txt builds ES-module output with MODULARIZE, EXPORT_ES6, environments web,worker,node, exceptions, memory growth, a 128 MiB initial heap and a 512 MiB maximum. The normal measured build uses -O1. The exported entry points are rosettatab_run_protocol, legacy rosettatab_run and main; ccall, filesystem and heap interfaces support the host.

The package has three scientific files:

  • rosetta.mjs: Emscripten factory/glue and preloaded-resource mapping.
  • rosetta.wasm: compiled scientific/runtime code.
  • rosetta.data: required database bytes mounted under /database in the virtual filesystem.

The engine with large-input memory adaptations totals 146,090,371 uncompressed bytes: 473,285 bytes of JavaScript glue, 117,465,890 bytes of WASM and 28,151,196 bytes of database resources. These sizes describe the scientific files rather than the private ZIP archive. Hashes identify the exact measured artifacts. Emscripten file packaging.

docs.title: 5. Cooperative scheduling and trajectory preservation
docs.text:
The browser ABI uses Asyncify so emscripten_sleep can yield to a worker's event loop. A hook between score evaluations measures active quanta and sleeps according to the requested duty target. It does not modify coordinates or consume random draws. Initialization is synchronous until the harness enables yielding. Emscripten Asyncify.

Generated static constructors/options registration, enum dictionaries, topology parsing and energy-table setup caused excessive VM compilation allocations when fully instrumented. The measured build excludes specific synchronous routines from Asyncify instrumentation while preserving it on scientific callers that can yield. Earlier full builds crashed; the bounded build passed normal Chrome/Brave VM checks. Diagnostic flags are not required by participants.

Atom-tree routines are also excluded from Asyncify: coordinate/domain-map traversal and destruction do not call the scientific pause or snapshot hooks. Instrumenting every recursive frame unnecessarily consumes the VM stack for larger proteins. Two WASM-only adaptations use heap worklists for atom release and domain-map traversal. The domain-map traversal preserves depth-first order and the parent's color changes before visiting the next sibling. Native retains the original recursive implementation for comparison.

This is cooperative execution within one worker, not a portable serializable continuation. Worker termination destroys that execution stack. The extension checkpoints completed models; the SDK caller must implement its own completed-work persistence.

docs.title: Startup and power budget
docs.text:
There are several different startup costs: fetching assets, compiling immutable WASM code, instantiating memory/filesystem, Rosetta core::init::init, importing the Pose and building/scoring energy tables. The first emitted scientific frame follows those preparation steps. A finished Emscripten factory or a responsive page therefore does not mean Rosetta is already warm.

In rosettatab_run_protocol, initialize(seed) currently runs before duty_percent and quantum_started are set. Later hooks yield after accumulated work of about 12 ms, sleeping in proportion to the requested duty target; long synchronous sections are not preempted. Display snapshot scoring itself also takes work. The intensity setting is an approximate cooperative budget, not a total-machine CPU or temperature limit.

Concurrent extension pools share a compiled module, while single-worker runs compile inside their worker. The extension terminates each model's instance on completion, so scientific initialization can recur for each model. The SDK keeps an instance warm across sequential calls. Comparative hardware and fan measurements have not established the cause of temperature differences between M-series laptops. Extension defaults are one worker/10%, with a 30-second rest between automatic network models. The standalone SDK defaults to 25% when the option is omitted; dutyCycle: 10 explicitly selects a lighter cooperative budget.

docs.title: Host memory boundary
docs.text:
packages/shared/src/wasm-bridge.ts UTF-8 encodes the complete PDB, allocates its bytes plus a NUL in the WASM heap, reads the current HEAPU8 after allocation, and calls the fixed ABI with a numeric pointer. The allocation remains live across Asyncify yields and is released in finally. This avoids copying a large upload onto the separate 1 MiB C stack. Memory growth replaces typed-array views; callers must not retain an old heap view across allocations. Emscripten C/JavaScript calls.

The final JSON string belongs to the harness's static response buffer. Parse/copy it before another call, and never enter the same module concurrently. Isolated workers provide separate scientific global state; JavaScript promises alone do not make Rosetta globals reentrant.

Source hook Snapshot meaning Harness before/after protocol Initial imported pose and final returned coordinates protocols/relax/FastRelax.cc Pose at fixed script-command boundaries core/optimization/AtomTreeMultifunc.cc Torsion minimizer pose synchronized after derivative evaluation core/optimization/CartesianMultifunc.cc Corresponding Cartesian derivative state core/pack/pack_rotamers.cc / FixbbSimAnnealer.cc Reconstruct a complete accepted rotamer assignment on a copy

The C++ display bridge copies the pose, removes unsuitable minimizer neighbor-list/cache state, independently scores the copy with full REF2015 and emits PDB/energy metadata through an EM_JS callback. Accepted packing assignments live in the annealer until committed, so the bridge reconstructs them on a copy instead of reading stale original coordinates. Internal updates are throttled to approximately one per 200 ms.

Display scoring does not alter the scientific pose or RNG. Recorded validation compares seeded results with the live bridge disabled and enabled. The bridge exposes calculation states without shortening minimizer steps or changing convergence to increase visual motion. Native Rosetta@home graphics use a separate shared-memory implementation. Pinned native graphics definition.

docs.title: 7. Standalone browser host
docs.text:
The standalone SDK uses the same scientific ABI and verified engine bytes. It validates the manifest and hashes, compiles the checked WASM buffer with WebAssembly.compile and supplies the supported instantiateWasm callback to the Emscripten factory. Verified database bytes enter through getPreloadedPackage. This factory does not accept Module.wasmBinary; the supported callback permits standalone hosting without modifying or rebuilding the Rosetta glue.

The SDK worker maps globalThis.rosettatabSnapshot to typed messages, validates final result identity and adds input/output hashes and timing scopes. One client owns one worker; distinct method imports route to the same fixed ABI. React, Nostr, extension permissions and native clients are absent from this layer. Emscripten C/JS interoperation.

docs.title: Validation boundaries
docs.text: Compilation is not proof of general scientific equivalence, arbitrary database support or official task acceptance. Native/WASM fixed-coordinate agreement and output rescoring are measured gates for recorded fixtures. Broader methods, chemistry, full workunit semantics, performance, project approval and public distribution each require their own evidence.

docs.title: Standalone quick start
docs.text:
@rotab/rosetta-wasm is a browser library for the eight bounded Rosetta coordinate methods. It runs in a dedicated module worker and is independent of the extension, volunteer network, and native clients.

The adapter currently has local package metadata at version 0.1.0 and has not been published to a package registry. Integration requires the generated adapter files and a matching, authorized scientific engine. The adapter's MIT license is separate from Rosetta's license. Build reference, licensing and availability.

docs.title: Use the package
docs.text:
The adapter is supplied as a local tarball for integration into a host application. If the application bundler does not preserve module workers and chunks, copy the package's complete dist/ to a static asset directory and supply workerUrl explicitly.

import { createRosetta, preparePdb } from "@rotab/rosetta-wasm";
import { relax } from "@rotab/rosetta-wasm/relax";

const client = createRosetta({
  engineUrl: new URL("/science/engine/", location.href),
  workerUrl: new URL("/science/sdk/worker.js", location.href),
});

const originalPdb = await (await fetch("/target.pdb")).text();
const prepared = preparePdb(originalPdb);
try {
  const result = await relax(client, prepared.pdb, {
    seed: 17,
    dutyCycle: 10,
    onPhase: phase => updateStatus(phase),
    onSnapshot: frame => {
      renderPdb(frame.pdb);
      appendEnergy(frame.energy); // REF2015 / REU
    },
  });
  saveRecord({ originalPdb, preparation: prepared.report, result });
} finally {
  client.close();
}

updateStatus, renderPdb, appendEnergy and saveRecord are application callbacks, not SDK exports. The provided vanilla example implements an energy graph and PDB/JSON download without a viewer dependency. Feed frame.pdb into Mol* or another viewer when embedding molecular rendering.

Alternatively call client.relax(pdb, options) or the generic client.run("relax", pdb, options). Every method shares the same pinned engine; separate imports do not duplicate its 146 MB scientific payload.

docs.title: Plain browser example
docs.text:
The private bundle's entry point is dist/rosetta-wasm-standalone/example/index.html. It includes input upload, method/seed/intensity selection, run/abort controls, measured energy history and result/provenance downloads. Deploy the directory as static HTTPS assets or mount it in an existing development preview. Participants access the application through a browser without installing a compiler, native helper or local service.

rosetta-wasm-standalone/
  example/index.html, main.js, input.pdb
  sdk/index.js, worker.js, chunks…, methods/…, *.d.ts
  engine/manifest.json, rosetta.mjs, rosetta.wasm, rosetta.data
  engine/ROSETTA_LICENSE.md, CITING_ROSETTA.md

Opening with file:// does not provide a suitable module/fetch origin. Serve .mjs/.js as JavaScript and .wasm as application/wasm. Keep generated chunks in place. The worker should be same-origin; cross-origin scientific assets require CORS. Typical CSP needs local scripts, worker-src 'self' and permission to compile WASM ('wasm-unsafe-eval' in script-src). No SharedArrayBuffer/pthread headers are required for this build.

Cold initialization can take minutes. The first Rosetta call performs lazy database and scoring-table setup after the Emscripten factory returns, so loading-module is not the whole cold-start cost. Reuse a client for sequential runs to retain that setup, and call close() when finished to release the heap. See API lifecycle and measured benchmarks.

This example explicitly requests 10% intensity; the SDK's omitted-option default remains 25%. The extension independently defaults to one worker/10%. For static deployment, cancellation, warm reuse and persistence responsibilities, follow Deployment and integration.

Sequence and residue IDs are preserved. There is no conformational search. Pose import can complete missing standard atoms or hydrogens; this is scoring after Rosetta import, not a promise of a byte-identical PDB.

The optimization/reporting score function is REF2015. objectiveEnergy precedes PDB rounding; the returned energy is independently evaluated on the returned rounded PDB coordinates.

docs.title: Live view
docs.text:
Score emits initial and final states without an optimization trajectory. Camera rotation and display motion do not represent relaxation.

Snapshots are visualization records, not execution checkpoints or physical time steps. Energy can rise between callbacks.

docs.title: Evidence and limits
docs.text:
Recorded native/Node and Chrome/Brave scientific checks use the first 20-residue 1L2Y model, seed 17, with independent rescoring of returned structures. Standalone SDK checks have their own scope in the evidence inventory. Shared engine validation does not establish an all-method standalone browser benchmark.

There is no relaxation, folding trajectory, custom weight set or external constraints interface. The separate 76-residue 1UBQ browser proof extends scoring input-size coverage, not all-protocol coverage.

All inputs remain subject to canonical single-chain chemistry and finite memory. BOINC workunit flags and official Rosetta@home result acceptance are outside this adapter.

The scientific harness engine/rosettatab.cc defines these settings; upstream reference documents the algorithm and source context.
